rationale: Mór-hop is a compound noun denoting a boggy, marshy hollow or retreat, as used in Beowulf (B. 450) to describe the fen-dwelling terrain of Grendel's lair. The only semantically appropriate candidate is marsh.n.01 (low-lying wet land with grassy vegetation), which matches the concrete, topographical sense of the gloss; the other candidates are proper nouns referring to individuals and are clearly inapplicable.
